> "It is easy to lie with statistics; it is easier to lie without them."
> — Frederick Mosteller

Statistics is one of the most powerful tools for understanding the world around us, especially within the context of crime and criminal justice. This course covers both **traditional (frequentist)** and **Bayesian** approaches to statistical reasoning, with all analysis done in **R**.

Everything for the course lives on this site:

- The [Schedule](schedule.qmd) — week-by-week topics, readings, slides, labs, and homework
- The [Syllabus](syllabus.qmd) — policies, grading, expectations
- [Resources](resources.qmd) — installing R and RStudio, datasets, textbook links

## Textbooks

- **Stanton**, *Reasoning with Data: An Introduction to Traditional and Bayesian Statistics Using R* (required)
- **Wickham, Çetinkaya-Rundel & Grolemund**, [*R for Data Science* (2nd edition)](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/) — free online (assigned readings woven through the first half of the course)

## Getting started

1. Install R and RStudio before the first class — [instructions here](resources.qmd#installing-r-and-rstudio)
2. Read the [Syllabus](syllabus.qmd)
3. Bring your laptop to **every** class meeting
